qt: to the Commission Stelios Kouloglou (The Left), Konstantinos Arvanitis (The Left), Malte Gallée (Verts/ALE), Francisco Guerreiro (Verts/ALE), José Gusmão (The Left), Marisa Matias (The Left), Silvia Modig (The Left), Ville Niinistö (Verts/ALE), Demetris Papadakis (S&D), Eugenia Rodríguez Palop (The Left), Ivan Vilibor Sinčić (NI), Tineke Strik (Verts/ALE) Subject:

Citizen groups from the Greek island of Ikaria are demanding the immediate closure and restoration of the island’s two uncontrolled waste disposal sites (landfills) in Evdilos and Raches1. A document sent from the Municipality of Ikaria to the Commission in 2021 announced the closure of the landfill. According to the relevant correspondence between Ikaria citizen groups and the Directorate-General for Environment, the landfills on Ikaria are considered closed for the rehabilitation of the sites. The reality is that, as the citizen groups documented with recent photos, the two landfills are still operating illegally and the municipal trucks drop off waste. The creation of a legal facility for the island’s municipal waste has been pending for more than 17 years, and Ikaria’s inclusion in the Solid Waste Management Agency of Chios was made solely for appearances and to appease EU regulators, without having any substantial effect. In this context: 1.
What does the Commission intend to do to ensure that the ongoing illegal operation of the uncontrolled waste disposal sites in Ikaria will finally cease?
How were the allegations that the landfill had been closed confirmed – falsely? And what are the direct implications of this?

(6 March 2024) On 2 December 2014 (2) the Court of Justice of the European Union condemned Greece for not having executed its first judgment in Commission v Greece on illegal landfills (3). The Court also imposed financial sanctions that Greece will have to pay until it can demonstrate that all illegal landfills covered by the ruling are closed and rehabilitated. As the Commission does not have inspection powers, it is up to Greece to send all necessary documentation (including official certificates of closure and rehabilitation) demonstrating that an illegal landfill has been closed and rehabilitated. Once the Greek authorities transmit such documentation, the Commission consider the illegal landfill as closed and/or rehabilitated. It cannot be excluded that some illegal landfills covered by the ruling resume operation, even though official certificates of closure have been granted. The Commission becomes aware of such situations through complaints and invites citizens to submit evidence available (e.g., an inspection report from a competent Greek authority) backing-up such a claim. Subsequently, the Commission raises the matter with the authorities. This has happened for another landfill in Greece but not, for the time being, for the landfill of Ikaria. If the evidence available shows that a similar problem occurs in Ikaria, the Commission will contact the Greek authorities and, where necessary, make the necessary adaptations to the semestrial fine that it will impose on Greece based on the above ruling of the Court.
